summary: Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (~1907–1911), Kōkōdō, and under Manshi Kiyozawa and Mahagoda Siri Nanissara. He later served as a professor at Otani University from 1919.

Chizuko Yoshimizu (b. 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at Gakushuin University, the University of Tokyo under Zuiho Yamaguchi, and the University of Vienna. She held faculty positions at the University of Tsukuba from 2003.
Chlodwig H. Werba (b. 1947) is an Indologist and linguist. He held academic posts as a professor at the University of Vienna, attested between 1997 and 2022.
Chogye Shabdrung (b. 1981) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 and under Sonam Gyatso.

Chogye Trichen Rinpoche (1920–2007) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 13th Dalai Lama, Geshe Tshechok, Kunga Chöphel, and Zimwok Rinpoche, and became the Eighteenth Chogye Trichen at Phenpo Nalendra Monastery in 1928.
Chogyu Takayama (1871–1902) was a scholar in philosophy and Japanology. He completed studies at Fukushima Prefectural Asaka High School (~1886–1891) and the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896).
Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and under traditional teacher Daehaeng Kun Sunim (attested 2012).
Choying Wangmo Dorji (1897–1994) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She founded the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and served as a member of its General Council from 1964 to 1965.
Chris Clark is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Sydney in 2015 under Mark Allon. He later served there as an honorary associate (attested 2019).
Chris Williams is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied and served as teaching staff at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Rita Langer (attested 2026).

Christian August Brandis (1790–1867) was a philosopher who studied at Kiel University (~1808–1812). He held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen (~1812–1815), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1816–1821), and the University of Bonn (~1821–1867).

Christian Bartholomae (1855–1925), a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, studied under Heinrich Hübschmann. He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1879–1885), Münster (~1885–1898), Giessen (~1898–1900), and Heidelberg (~1909–1924).

Christian Bernert is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen (1791–1860) was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Marburg, Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, Munich, Leiden, Copenhagen, and under Silvestre de Sacy, founding the German Archaeological Institute in 1829.

Christian Coseru is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Bucharest and the Australian National University, and became an Associate Professor of Philosophy at the College of Charleston around 2006.

Christian Friedrich August Dillmann (1823–1894) specialized in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Tübingen under Heinrich Ewald and held posts at Tübingen (~1848–1854), Kiel (~1854–1864), Giessen (~1864–1869), and Frederick William University Berlin (~1869–1894).

Christian Gottlob Heyne (1729–1812) was a linguistics and history scholar who studied at the University of Leipzig. In 1763 he became a professor at the University of Göttingen, where he also served as library director from 1764 to 1812.

Christian K. Wedemeyer (b. 1969), a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, studied at Wesleyan and Columbia. He held posts at Copenhagen (2000–2003) and the University of Chicago (2003–2011).

Christian Lassen (1800–1876) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Oslo, Heidelberg, and Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He taught at the University of Bonn as Privatdozent (1830) and professor of Old Indian language and literature (1840–1876).

Christian Lee Novetzke (b. 1969) is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Macalester, Harvard, and Columbia. He taught at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) before becoming Director of the South Asia Center at the University of Washington in 2007.
